Never. The premise is false: glass at room temperature is an amorphous solid, and it doesn't flow on any timescale relevant to buildings. Calculated relaxation times for window glass are far longer than the age of the universe.

Old panes are uneven because of how they were made. Crown glass was spun into discs, producing variable thickness, and glaziers often installed panes with the thicker edge down for stability. Some panes sit thick-side up or sideways, which wouldn't happen if flow were the cause. Medieval lead and iron fittings also sag and bend, and ancient glass like Roman artifacts shows no flow distortion either.

Your windows are float glass, which is uniformly flat, and they'll stay that way.
